# ots.golf

> A competition on the worst-case verification cost, in compressions, of hash-based one-time
> signatures with a 128-bit public key, signatures of at most 5504 bits and 127-bit security.
> Three lower classes and one Upper bound track are open. Certificates are checked by the Lean kernel.

Public tracks, from broadest to most restricted lower class:

| Track | Slug | Schemes | Checked claim |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Generality 3/3 | generic-lower | Any admissible oracle algorithm | 1 |
| Generality 2/3 | lower | Fixed DAGs with arbitrary deterministic functions and disclosure cuts | 18 |
| Generality 1/3 | disclosure-lower | Whole-word DAGs: 128-bit secrets, 256-bit hashes, fixed halves and concatenation | 93 |
| Upper bound | generic-upper | Any admissible oracle algorithm | 106 |

Lower claims are universal within their class; larger is better. Upper claims construct a scheme;
smaller is better. Each lower class has its own record. The Upper bound
certificate proves perfect correctness, signing failure at most 2^-128, 127-bit strong security,
all resource limits and a worst-case verification cost of 106 compressions. Generality 3/3 lower
uses the same signing-failure limit of 2^-128 and weak unforgeability. Both availability requirements
are averaged over honest key generation and signing for every public-key-dependent message choice.

All parties share one random oracle on bit strings, returning 256 bits. Equal inputs always share
an answer across all uses. Input lengths include explicit parameters and tweaks. Each query
costs one compression per started 512-bit input block, at least one.
Messages are 256 bits; key generation costs at most 1024 compressions and signing at most 2^21.
Deterministic computation and randomness are free. The protected Lean interfaces define the exact
security experiments; AGENTS.md lists submission requirements.

Submission roots are formal/Submissions/GenericLower, Lower, DisclosureLower and GenericUpper,
respectively. The Upper and DisclosureUpper roots remain historical reference certificates at
106, with closed public admission.

Submit a pull request changing only one admitted submission root. It must be flat, include
Solution.lean and claim.txt, obey import and size limits, and use the pinned toolchain. Exported
proofs may use only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice: no sorry or native_decide.
Optional PR-body lines `Assisted by: <model>` and `Co-authors: a, b` provide attribution.
A verified improvement becomes a record only when that exact head is merged.

Local checks, replacing generic-upper with another track slug as needed:

    verifier/setup_tools.sh
    cd formal && lake exe cache get && lake build OptimalOTS Submissions
    cd ..
    python3 verifier/check_submission.py generic-upper
    python3 verifier/verify.py generic-upper --source .

macOS proof checks run unsandboxed for trusted local development. Production requires the Linux isolation
and launch checks in service/deploy/README.md. Lower filters affect only lower leaderboards;
the chart has three lower series and one Upper bound series. Rules contain no current scores.
Local Satoshi/Vitalik rows are clearly fictional demos, never verified submissions; preserve them
and refresh localhost after commits. Never push or deploy without authorization.

- Repository: https://github.com/TomWambsgans/ots.golf (site: https://ots.golf)
- Exact submission requirements and exports: AGENTS.md
- Track metadata, limits and protected files: challenges.json
- Interfaces: formal/OptimalOTS/{Algorithm,AlgorithmWeak,Statement,WholeWords}.lean
- Proof guides: docs/{generic-lower,lower-bound-proof,whole-words,generic-upper}.md
- Official verifier: verifier/verify.py
